hook_text: In 1750 a weaver in an English cottage spent half his time doing nothing. That waiting started the Industrial Revolution.
clip_script: England, 1750. A merchant drops off a bag of wool at a cottage. The children comb it, the mother spins it into thread at a wheel by the fire, and the father weaves it into cloth on a wooden loom. That is the domestic system. But here is the problem: one weaver needs the thread of several spinners, so the father keeps waiting for thread. Meanwhile, outside, the village is changing. Rich landowners are fencing off the old strip fields and the common land. That is enclosure. Farms grow more food, but poor families lose their land and walk to the towns looking for work. Now put it together. A shortage of thread, a crowd of people needing jobs, and merchants with money to invest. Whoever builds a machine that spins faster will make a fortune. And somebody did. That is how the Industrial Revolution began.
visual_style: A whiteboard cottage with a spinning wheel and loom, a clock ticking while the weaver waits, then a village map with fences closing in around strip fields and arrows of people walking towards a distant town.
pacing: Gentle opening scene, a sharp beat on the waiting weaver, a building sequence to the payoff.
